forecasts.reason: The epoch dial gives about 0.1 pp and 5% time per 0.5 epoch, but the RNG re-roll adds ±0.3 pp of noise, so the 0.753 bar is a coin flip.
26 px cuts about 14% of pixels in 30% of steps, which saves about 1.5% of time. The accuracy change is below the noise.
The change is time-neutral. Any accuracy effect is within noise, and an untested averaging schedule is more likely to be flat than to give +0.3 pp.
Label smoothing was flat within noise in E013, so a per-phase split is unlikely to show a resolvable effect.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change, so the tip's numbers are unchanged. It will likely show some low-efficiency layers, which would explain why E021 returned only part of its MAC savings.
The 4000-image candidate forward pass plus the proxy cost likely outweigh the savings in a compute-bound short run. Time is more likely to rise than to fall 5%.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 10-seed mean accuracy on held-out seeds? If it is below 0.752, every further trim fails the bar and a free accuracy lever is needed first.
Is any accuracy lever (averaging schedule, BN recalibration, label smoothing per phase) resolvable above the ±0.3 pp 3-seed noise? Only a lever worth at least 0.3 pp can pay for further time trims.
Do architecture cuts such as group-2 width or conv count save time at less accuracy cost per second than the epoch dial? The profile of per-layer efficiency decides this.
